title: Run one command on several servers over SSH and save each result
summary: Read a list of servers, run the same command on each one over SSH, save every output in its own file, and print which servers failed. Use it for read-only checks such as uptime or free disk space.

aliases.text: run command on multiple servers ssh
run same command on many hosts
ssh to several servers at once
gather output from many ssh hosts
выполнить команду на нескольких серверах по ssh

steps.explain: Save the script from the script section and make it executable. It reads the host list, runs your command on each host over SSH, and saves each host's output in its own file.
Write the host list, one name per line. The names can be ssh config aliases or IP addresses. Set up key-based login first: the script never types a password.

placeholders.name: HOSTS_FILE
placeholders.description: Text file with one host per line

steps.explain: Test the connection to one host first. 'reachable' means the key login works. 'Permission denied (publickey)' means the key is not on that host yet.

placeholders.name: HOST
placeholders.description: One host name from the host list

steps.explain: Run the command on every host. Use a read-only command such as uptime. Each host prints OK or FAIL, and the last line counts the failures.
steps.expect: Lines 'OK    web1.lan' or 'FAIL  ...', then 'failed hosts: 0' when all worked.

placeholders.name: HOSTS_FILE
placeholders.description: Text file with one host per line

placeholders.name: OUT_DIR
placeholders.description: Folder that receives one .out and one .err file per host

steps.explain: Read the results. The .out files hold each host's output; the .err files hold the error text of failed hosts.
steps.expect: One block of output per host. Errors such as 'Connection timed out' appear only in .err files.

warnings: The command runs under your account on every host in the list. Use only read-only commands unless you intend a change everywhere.

script.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
# Run one command on every host in HOSTS_FILE over ssh and save each result.
# Usage: collect.sh HOSTS_FILE OUT_DIR COMMAND
HOSTS_FILE="${1:?usage: $0 HOSTS_FILE OUT_DIR COMMAND}"
OUT_DIR="${2:?missing OUT_DIR}"
CMD="${3:?missing COMMAND}"
mkdir -p "$OUT_DIR"
fail=0
while IFS= read -r host || [[ -n "$host" ]]; do
  [[ -z "$host" || "$host" == \#* ]] && continue
  if timeout 60 ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=10 "$host" "$CMD" > "$OUT_DIR/$host.out" 2> "$OUT_DIR/$host.err"; then
    echo "OK    $host"
  else
    rc=$?
    echo "FAIL  $host (exit $rc, see $OUT_DIR/$host.err)"
    fail=$((fail + 1))
  fi
done < "$HOSTS_FILE"
echo "failed hosts: $fail"
[[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]]
